### Bug report

```
matplotlib/lib/matplotlib/axes/_base.py:

/.../
def set_xlim(...)
/.../
        if emit:
            self.callbacks.process('xlim_changed', self)
            # Call all of the other x-axes that are shared with this one

                    other.set_xlim(self.viewLim.intervalx,

```

I'm very new to matplotlib, so perhaps there is a good reason for this? emit=False seems to disable both continued "inheritance" of axis (why?) and triggering of change callbacks (looking at the code above).

It seems like one would at least want to trigger the xlim_changed callbacks as they would be intended to react to any change in axis limits.

Edit: Setting emit=True seems to introduce a recursion issue (not sure why but as inheritance seems to be passed along anyway it doesn't really matter). ``struct.Struct`` is implemented in the private ``_struct`` module, so its

{"content": """"Regression tests for the ``struct.Struct`` type annotation (issue #8410).

``struct.Struct`` is implemented in the private ``_struct`` module, so its
``__module__`` attribute is ``'_struct'`` while the documented and
cross-referenceable name is ``struct.Struct``.  Sphinx used to stringify the
annotation using ``__module__`` and emitted ``_struct.Struct``, which could not
be resolved (``class reference target not found: Struct`` with ``-n``).
"""

import importlib.util
import struct
from pathlib import Path
from types import TracebackType

from sphinx.util.inspect import signature, stringify_signature
from sphinx.util.typing import get_type_hints, stringify

TARGET = '''\
import pathlib
import struct


def consume_struct(_: struct.Struct) -> None:
    pass


def make_struct() -> struct.Struct:
    return struct.Struct('HH')


def make_path() -> pathlib.Path:
    return pathlib.Path()
'''


def consume_struct(_: struct.Struct) -> None:
    pass


def make_struct() -> struct.Struct:
    return struct.Struct('HH')


def test_stringify_struct() -> None:
    assert stringify(struct.Struct) == 'struct.Struct'


def test_stringify_traceback_type() -> None:
    assert stringify(TracebackType) == 'types.TracebackType'


def test_stringify_signature_with_struct_annotation() -> None:
    sig = signature(consume_struct)
    assert 'struct.Struct' in stringify_signature(sig)
    assert '_struct.Struct' not in stringify_signature(sig)

    sig = signature(make_struct)
    assert stringify_signature(sig).endswith('-> struct.Struct')
    assert '_struct' not in stringify_signature(sig)


def test_annotation_pipeline_of_a_module(tmp_path) -> None:
    """Resolved annotations of a real module are stringified with public names.

    This is the pipeline used by autodoc to render signatures: the annotations
    are evaluated by ``typing.get_type_hints()`` (wrapped by Sphinx) and then
    stringified by ``sphinx.util.typing.stringify()``.
    """
    target = tmp_path / 'target.py'
    target.write_text(TARGET)

    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('regression_target', str(target))
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)

    hints = get_type_hints(module.consume_struct)
    assert stringify(hints['_']) == 'struct.Struct'

    # pathlib.Path keeps working (its __module__ is already correct)
    hints = get_type_hints(module.make_path)
    assert stringify(hints['return']) == 'pathlib.Path'

    assert stringify_signature(signature(module.consume_struct)) == \
        '(_: struct.Struct) -> None'
    assert stringify_signature(signature(module.make_struct)) == '() -> struct.Struct'

import sys
from numbers import Integral
from typing import (Any, Callable, Dict, Generator, List, NewType, Optional, Tuple, TypeVar,
                    Union)

import pytest

from sphinx.util.typing import restify, stringify


class MyClass1:
    pass


class MyClass2(MyClass1):
    __qualname__ = '<MyClass2>'


T = TypeVar('T')
MyInt = NewType('MyInt', int)


class MyList(List[T]):
    pass


class BrokenType:
    __args__ = int


def test_restify():
    assert restify(int) == ":class:`int`"
    assert restify(str) == ":class:`str`"
    assert restify(None) == ":obj:`None`"
    assert restify(Integral) == ":class:`numbers.Integral`"
    assert restify(Any) == ":obj:`Any`"


def test_restify_type_hints_containers():
    assert restify(List) == ":class:`List`"
    assert restify(Dict) == ":class:`Dict`"
    assert restify(List[int]) == ":class:`List`\\ [:class:`int`]"
    assert restify(List[str]) == ":class:`List`\\ [:class:`str`]"
    assert restify(Dict[str, float]) == ":class:`Dict`\\ [:class:`str`, :class:`float`]"
    assert restify(Tuple[str, str, str]) == ":class:`Tuple`\\ [:class:`str`, :class:`str`, :class:`str`]"
    assert restify(Tuple[str, ...]) == ":class:`Tuple`\\ [:class:`str`, ...]"
    assert restify(List[Dict[str, Tuple]]) == ":class:`List`\\ [:class:`Dict`\\ [:class:`str`, :class:`Tuple`]]"
    assert restify(MyList[Tuple[int, int]]) == ":class:`tests.test_util_typing.MyList`\\ [:class:`Tuple`\\ [:class:`int`, :class:`int`]]"
    assert restify(Generator[None, None, None]) == ":class:`Generator`\\ [:obj:`None`, :obj:`None`, :obj:`None`]"


def test_restify_type_hints_Callable():
    assert restify(Callable) == ":class:`Callable`"

    if sys.version_info >= (3, 7):
        assert restify(Callable[[str], int]) == ":class:`Callable`\\ [[:class:`str`], :class:`int`]"
        assert restify(Callable[..., int]) == ":class:`Callable`\\ [[...], :class:`int`]"
    else:
        assert restify(Callable[[str], int]) == ":class:`Callable`\\ [:class:`str`, :class:`int`]"
        assert restify(Callable[..., int]) == ":class:`Callable`\\ [..., :class:`int`]"


def test_restify_type_hints_Union():

## 修复完成

### 问题根因
`sphinx/environment/adapters/indexentries.py` 的 `keyfunc` 排序键中，字母条目加前缀 `chr(127)`（0x7F），而符号条目保留原始首字符不加前缀。因此码点小于 0x7F 的符号（`@`）排在字母之前，码点大于 0x7F 的符号（`£`、`←`）排在字母之后。`groupby` 只能合并相邻同组条目，非连续的符号条目被切成两个 "Symbols" 分组 → HTML 中出现两个 `Symbols` 标题、两个 `#Symbols` 跳转链接且都指向第一个锚点。

### 修改
`sphinx/environment/adapters/indexentries.py`（唯一实现改动，第 111-120 行）：符号条目也加一个低于 `chr(127)` 的前缀，使所有符号条目排在字母之前并彼此相邻：

```python
if lckey[0:1].isalpha() or lckey.startswith('_'):
    lckey = chr(127) + lckey
else:
    lckey = chr(0) + lckey   # 符号统一排在字母前，避免拆成两个 Symbols 段
```

新增回归测试 `regressions/test_index_symbols_grouping.py`（`regressions/` 下直接新建，未改动任何受保护文件/目录）：
- 单元级：`@`、`£`、`←` + 字母条目 → 仅一个 `Symbols` 分组且位于最前，含全部三个符号；

def assert_re_search(regex: Pattern, text: str, flags: int = 0) -> None:
    if not re.search(regex, text, flags):
        assert False, '%r did not match %r' % (regex, text)


def assert_not_re_search(regex: Pattern, text: str, flags: int = 0) -> None:
    if re.search(regex, text, flags):
        assert False, '%r did match %r' % (regex, text)


def assert_startswith(thing: str, prefix: str) -> None:
    if not thing.startswith(prefix):
        assert False, '%r does not start with %r' % (thing, prefix)


def assert_node(node: Node, cls: Any = None, xpath: str = "", **kwargs: Any) -> None:
    if cls:
        if isinstance(cls, list):
            assert_node(node, cls[0], xpath=xpath, **kwargs)
            if cls[1:]:
                if isinstance(cls[1], tuple):
                    assert_node(node, cls[1], xpath=xpath, **kwargs)
                else:
                    assert isinstance(node, nodes.Element), \
                        'The node%s does not have any children' % xpath
                    assert len(node) == 1, \
                        'The node%s has %d child nodes, not one' % (xpath, len(node))
                    assert_node(node[0], cls[1:], xpath=xpath + "[0]", **kwargs)
        elif isinstance(cls, tuple):
            assert isinstance(node, (list, nodes.Element)), \
                'The node%s does not have any items' % xpath
            assert len(node) == len(cls), \
                'The node%s has %d child nodes, not %r' % (xpath, len(node), len(cls))
            for i, nodecls in enumerate(cls):
                path = xpath + "[%d]" % i
                assert_node(node[i], nodecls, xpath=path, **kwargs)
        elif isinstance(cls, str):
            assert node == cls, 'The node %r is not %r: %r' % (xpath, cls, node)
        else:
            assert isinstance(node, cls), \
                'The node%s is not subclass of %r: %r' % (xpath, cls, node)

    if kwargs:
        assert isinstance(node, nodes.Element), \
            'The node%s does not have any attributes' % xpath

        for key, value in kwargs.items():
            assert key in node, \
                'The node%s does not have %r attribute: %r' % (xpath, key, node)
            assert node[key] == value, \
                'The node%s[%s] is not %r: %r' % (xpath, key, value, node[key])

{"file_path": "/workspace/regressions/test_index_symbols_grouping.py", "content": """"
    test_index_symbols_grouping
    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

    Regression tests for index entry grouping.

    Index entries whose keys start with a symbol that sorts after ASCII
    letters (e.g. ``£`` or ``←``) used to end up in a *second* "Symbols"
    section, after the letter sections.  The HTML output then contained two
    ``Symbols`` headings and two jumpbox links pointing at the same anchor.

    :copyright: Copyright 2007-2020 by the Sphinx team, see AUTHORS.
    :license: BSD, see LICENSE for details.
"""

from io import StringIO

from sphinx.application import Sphinx
from sphinx.environment.adapters.indexentries import IndexEntries


class _FakeBuilder:
    def get_relative_uri(self, from_, to):
        return 'genindex.html'


class _FakeDomain:
    def __init__(self, entries):
        self.entries = entries


class _FakeEnv:
    def __init__(self, entries):
        self._domain = _FakeDomain(entries)

    def get_domain(self, name):
        assert name == 'index'
        return self._domain


def _create_index(entries):
    env = _FakeEnv({'index': entries})
    return IndexEntries(env).create_index(_FakeBuilder())


def test_symbols_are_grouped_into_single_section():
    entries = [
        ('single', 'normal', 'index-0', '', None),
        ('single', '@', 'index-1', '', None),
        ('single', '£', 'index-2', '', None),
        ('single', '←', 'index-3', '', None),
        ('single', 'Zebra', 'index-4', '', None),
    ]
    index = _create_index(entries)

    keys = [key for key, _entries in index]
    assert keys.count('Symbols') == 1
    assert keys == ['Symbols', 'N', 'Z']

    symbols = dict(index)['Symbols']
    assert [name for name, _entry in symbols] == ['@', '£', '←']


def test_genindex_html_contains_single_symbols_section(tmp_path):
    srcdir = tmp_path / 'src'
    srcdir.mkdir()
    (srcdir / 'conf.py').write_text(
        "master_doc = 'index'\n"
        "project = 'regression'\n"
        "html_theme = 'basic'\n",
        encoding='utf-8')
    (srcdir / 'index.rst').write_text(
        "Index\n"
        "=====\n"
        "\n"
        ".. index:: @\n"
        ".. index:: £\n"
        ".. index:: ←\n"
        ".. index:: normal\n",
        encoding='utf-8')

    outdir = tmp_path / 'out'
    doctreedir = tmp_path / 'doctrees'
    app = Sphinx(str(srcdir), str(srcdir), str(outdir), str(doctreedir), 'html',
                 status=StringIO(), warning=StringIO(), freshenv=True)
    app.build()

    html = (outdir / 'genindex.html').read_text(encoding='utf-8')
    assert html.count('id="Symbols"') == 1
    assert html.count('href="#Symbols"') == 1

    # every symbol entry is listed inside the single "Symbols" section
    symbols_section = html.split('id="Symbols"', 1)[1].split('<h2', 1)[0]
    for name in ('@', '£', '←'):
        assert name in symbols_section
    assert 'normal' not in symbols_section
"}

## 修复完成

### 问题根因
`sphinx/environment/adapters/indexentries.py` 的 `keyfunc` 排序键中，字母条目加前缀 `chr(127)`（0x7F），而符号条目保留原始首字符不加前缀。因此码点小于 0x7F 的符号（`@`）排在字母之前，码点大于 0x7F 的符号（`£`、`←`）排在字母之后。`groupby` 只能合并相邻同组条目，非连续的符号条目被切成两个 "Symbols" 分组 → HTML 中出现两个 `Symbols` 标题、两个 `#Symbols` 跳转链接且都指向第一个锚点。

### 修改
`sphinx/environment/adapters/indexentries.py`（唯一实现改动，第 111-120 行）：符号条目也加一个低于 `chr(127)` 的前缀，使所有符号条目排在字母之前并彼此相邻：

```python
if lckey[0:1].isalpha() or lckey.startswith('_'):
    lckey = chr(127) + lckey
else:
    lckey = chr(0) + lckey   # 符号统一排在字母前，避免拆成两个 Symbols 段
```

"""
import functools
import os
import re
import sys
import warnings
from io import StringIO
from typing import Any, Dict, Generator, IO, List, Pattern
from xml.etree import ElementTree

from docutils import nodes
from docutils.nodes import Node
from docutils.parsers.rst import directives, roles

def assert_re_search(regex: Pattern, text: str, flags: int = 0) -> None:
    if not re.search(regex, text, flags):
        assert False, '%r did not match %r' % (regex, text)


def assert_not_re_search(regex: Pattern, text: str, flags: int = 0) -> None:
    if re.search(regex, text, flags):
        assert False, '%r did match %r' % (regex, text)


def assert_startswith(thing: str, prefix: str) -> None:
    if not thing.startswith(prefix):
        assert False, '%r does not start with %r' % (thing, prefix)


def assert_node(node: Node, cls: Any = None, xpath: str = "", **kwargs: Any) -> None:
    if cls:
        if isinstance(cls, list):
            assert_node(node, cls[0], xpath=xpath, **kwargs)
            if cls[1:]:
                if isinstance(cls[1], tuple):
                    assert_node(node, cls[1], xpath=xpath, **kwargs)
                else:
                    assert isinstance(node, nodes.Element), \
                        'The node%s does not have any children' % xpath
                    assert len(node) == 1, \
                        'The node%s has %d child nodes, not one' % (xpath, len(node))
                    assert_node(node[0], cls[1:], xpath=xpath + "[0]", **kwargs)
        elif isinstance(cls, tuple):
            assert isinstance(node, (list, nodes.Element)), \
                'The node%s does not have any items' % xpath
            assert len(node) == len(cls), \
                'The node%s has %d child nodes, not %r' % (xpath, len(node), len(cls))
            for i, nodecls in enumerate(cls):
                path = xpath + "[%d]" % i
                assert_node(node[i], nodecls, xpath=path, **kwargs)
        elif isinstance(cls, str):
            assert node == cls, 'The node %r is not %r: %r' % (xpath, cls, node)
        else:
            assert isinstance(node, cls), \
                'The node%s is not subclass of %r: %r' % (xpath, cls, node)

    if kwargs:
        assert isinstance(node, nodes.Element), \
            'The node%s does not have any attributes' % xpath

        for key, value in kwargs.items():
            assert key in node, \
                'The node%s does not have %r attribute: %r' % (xpath, key, node)
            assert node[key] == value, \
                'The node%s[%s] is not %r: %r' % (xpath, key, value, node[key])


def etree_parse(path: str) -> Any:
    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=False):

"""

    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

    :copyright: Copyright 2007-2020 by the Sphinx team, see AUTHORS.
    :license: BSD, see LICENSE for details.
"""

from os import path

from docutils import nodes
from docutils.core import publish_doctree

from sphinx.application import Sphinx
from sphinx.io import SphinxStandaloneReader
from sphinx.parsers import RSTParser
from sphinx.util.docutils import sphinx_domains


def parse(app: Sphinx, text: str, docname: str = 'index') -> nodes.document:
    """Parse a string as reStructuredText with Sphinx application."""
    try:
        app.env.temp_data['docname'] = docname
        reader = SphinxStandaloneReader()
        reader.setup(app)
        parser = RSTParser()
        parser.set_application(app)
        with sphinx_domains(app.env):
            return publish_doctree(text, path.join(app.srcdir, docname + '.rst'),
                                   reader=reader,
                                   parser=parser,
                                   settings_overrides={'env': app.env,
                                                       'gettext_compact': True})
    finally:
        app.env.temp_data.pop('docname', None)

Release 3.2.0 (in development)
==============================

Dependencies
------------

Incompatible changes
--------------------

Deprecated
----------

* C, parsing of pre-v3 style type directives and roles, along with the options
  :confval:`c_allow_pre_v3` and :confval:`c_warn_on_allowed_pre_v3`.

Features added
--------------

* #2076: autodoc: Allow overriding of exclude-members in skip-member function
* #7849: html: Add :confval:`html_codeblock_linenos_style` to change the style
  of line numbers for code-blocks
* #7853: C and C++, support parameterized GNU style attributes.
* #7888: napoleon: Add aliases Warn and Raise.
* C, added :rst:dir:`c:alias` directive for inserting copies
  of existing declarations.
* #7745: html: inventory is broken if the docname contains a space
* #7902: html theme: Add a new option :confval:`globaltoc_maxdepth` to control
  the behavior of globaltoc in sidebar
* #7052: add ``:noindexentry:`` to the Python, C, C++, and Javascript domains.
  Update the documentation to better reflect the relationship between this option
  and the ``:noindex:`` option.
* #7899: C, add possibility of parsing of some pre-v3 style type directives and
  roles and try to convert them to equivalent v3 directives/roles.
  Set the new option :confval:`c_allow_pre_v3` to ``True`` to enable this.
  The warnings printed from this functionality can be suppressed by setting
  :confval:`c_warn_on_allowed_pre_v3`` to ``True``.
  The functionality is immediately deprecated.

Bugs fixed
----------

* #7886: autodoc: TypeError is raised on mocking generic-typed classes
* #7935: autodoc: function signature is not shown when the function has a
  parameter having ``inspect._empty`` as its default value
* #7901: autodoc: type annotations for overloaded functions are not resolved
* #904: autodoc: An instance attribute cause a crash of autofunction directive
* #1362: autodoc: ``private-members`` option does not work for class attributes
* #7839: autosummary: cannot handle umlauts in function names
* #7865: autosummary: Failed to extract summary line when abbreviations found
* #7866: autosummary: Failed to extract correct summary line when docstring
  contains a hyperlink target
* #7469: autosummary: "Module attributes" header is not translatable
* #7940: apidoc: An extra newline is generated at the end of the rst file if a
  module has submodules 
* #4258: napoleon: decorated special methods are not shown
* #7715: LaTeX: ``numfig_secnum_depth > 1`` leads to wrong figure links
* #7846: html theme: XML-invalid files were generated
* #7894: gettext: Wrong source info is shown when using rst_epilog
* #7691: linkcheck: HEAD requests are not used for checking
* #7928: py domain: failed to resolve a type annotation for the attribute
* #7968: i18n: The content of ``math`` directive is interpreted as reST on
  translation
* #7869: :rst:role:`abbr` role without an explanation will show the explanation
  from the previous abbr role
* C and C++, removed ``noindex`` directive option as it did
  nothing.
* #7619: Duplicated node IDs are generated if node has multiple IDs

Testing
--------

{"file_path": "/workspace/regressions/test_index_symbols.py", "content": """"Regression tests for grouping of symbol index entries.

See: "Two sections called Symbols in index".  Symbol entries whose leading
character lies after the ASCII letters (such as ``£`` and ``←``) used to be
sorted *after* the alphabetic entries, which produced a second ``Symbols``
group with the same HTML anchor as the first one.
"""

import pytest

from sphinx.environment.adapters.indexentries import IndexEntries
from sphinx.testing import restructuredtext
from sphinx.testing.path import path

pytest_plugins = 'sphinx.testing.fixtures'


@pytest.fixture(scope='session')
def rootdir():
    return path(__file__).parent.parent / 'tests' / 'roots'


@pytest.mark.sphinx('dummy', freshenv=True)
def test_symbols_are_grouped_into_single_section(app):
    text = (".. index:: @decorator\n"
            ".. index:: £pound\n"
            ".. index:: ←arrow\n"
            ".. index:: docutils\n")
    restructuredtext.parse(app, text)
    index = IndexEntries(app.env).create_index(app.builder)

    keys = [key for key, _ in index]
    # all symbol entries must share one single "Symbols" section
    assert keys.count('Symbols') == 1
    # ... and that section has to come before the alphabetic ones
    assert keys[0] == 'Symbols'
    assert keys[1] == 'D'

    symbols = dict(index)['Symbols']
    assert [name for name, _ in symbols] == ['@decorator', '£pound', '←arrow']


@pytest.mark.sphinx('dummy', freshenv=True)
def test_symbols_grouping_matches_low_ascii_symbols(app):
    text = (".. index:: 9-symbol\n"
            ".. index:: &-symbol\n"
            ".. index:: £-symbol\n"
            ".. index:: docutils\n")
    restructuredtext.parse(app, text)
    index = IndexEntries(app.env).create_index(app.builder)

    keys = [key for key, _ in index]
    assert keys == ['Symbols', 'D']
    symbols = dict(index)['Symbols']
    assert [name for name, _ in symbols] == ['&-symbol', '9-symbol', '£-symbol']
"}

    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

import functools
import os
import re
import sys
import warnings

from docutils import nodes
from docutils.nodes import Node
from docutils.parsers.rst import directives, roles

from sphinx.deprecation import RemovedInSphinx40Warning

def assert_re_search(regex: Pattern, text: str, flags: int = 0) -> None:
    if not re.search(regex, text, flags):
        assert False, '%r did not match %r' % (regex, text)


def assert_not_re_search(regex: Pattern, text: str, flags: int = 0) -> None:
    if re.search(regex, text, flags):
        assert False, '%r did match %r' % (regex, text)


def assert_startswith(thing: str, prefix: str) -> None:
    if not thing.startswith(prefix):
        assert False, '%r does not start with %r' % (thing, prefix)


def assert_node(node: Node, cls: Any = None, xpath: str = "", **kwargs: Any) -> None:
    if cls:
        if isinstance(cls, list):
            assert_node(node, cls[0], xpath=xpath, **kwargs)
            if cls[1:]:
                if isinstance(cls[1], tuple):
                    assert_node(node, cls[1], xpath=xpath, **kwargs)
                else:
                    assert isinstance(node, nodes.Element), \
                        'The node%s does not have any children' % xpath
                    assert len(node) == 1, \
                        'The node%s has %d child nodes, not one' % (xpath, len(node))
                    assert_node(node[0], cls[1:], xpath=xpath + "[0]", **kwargs)
        elif isinstance(cls, tuple):
            assert isinstance(node, (list, nodes.Element)), \
                'The node%s does not have any items' % xpath
            assert len(node) == len(cls), \
                'The node%s has %d child nodes, not %r' % (xpath, len(node), len(cls))
            for i, nodecls in enumerate(cls):
                path = xpath + "[%d]" % i
                assert_node(node[i], nodecls, xpath=path, **kwargs)
        elif isinstance(cls, str):
            assert node == cls, 'The node %r is not %r: %r' % (xpath, cls, node)
        else:
            assert isinstance(node, cls), \
                'The node%s is not subclass of %r: %r' % (xpath, cls, node)

    if kwargs:
        assert isinstance(node, nodes.Element), \
            'The node%s does not have any attributes' % xpath

        for key, value in kwargs.items():
            assert key in node, \
                'The node%s does not have %r attribute: %r' % (xpath, key, node)
            assert node[key] == value, \
                'The node%s[%s] is not %r: %r' % (xpath, key, value, node[key])


def etree_parse(path: str) -> Any:
    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=False):
        warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=DeprecationWarning)
        return ElementTree.parse(path)


class Struct:
    def __init__(self, **kwargs: Any) -> None:

"""
    sphinx.testing.restructuredtext
    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

    :copyright: Copyright 2007-2020 by the Sphinx team, see AUTHORS.
    :license: BSD, see LICENSE for details.
"""

from os import path

from docutils import nodes
from docutils.core import publish_doctree

from sphinx.application import Sphinx
from sphinx.io import SphinxStandaloneReader
from sphinx.parsers import RSTParser
from sphinx.util.docutils import sphinx_domains


def parse(app: Sphinx, text: str, docname: str = 'index') -> nodes.document:
    """Parse a string as reStructuredText with Sphinx application."""
    try:
        app.env.temp_data['docname'] = docname
        reader = SphinxStandaloneReader()
        reader.setup(app)
        parser = RSTParser()
        parser.set_application(app)
        with sphinx_domains(app.env):
            return publish_doctree(text, path.join(app.srcdir, docname + '.rst'),
                                   reader=reader,
                                   parser=parser,
                                   settings_overrides={'env': app.env,
                                                       'gettext_compact': True})
    finally:
        app.env.temp_data.pop('docname', None)

Release 3.2.0 (in development)
==============================

Dependencies
------------

Incompatible changes
--------------------

Deprecated
----------

* C, parsing of pre-v3 style type directives and roles, along with the options
  :confval:`c_allow_pre_v3` and :confval:`c_warn_on_allowed_pre_v3`.

Features added
--------------

* #2076: autodoc: Allow overriding of exclude-members in skip-member function
* #7849: html: Add :confval:`html_codeblock_linenos_style` to change the style
  of line numbers for code-blocks
* #7853: C and C++, support parameterized GNU style attributes.
* #7888: napoleon: Add aliases Warn and Raise.
* C, added :rst:dir:`c:alias` directive for inserting copies
  of existing declarations.
* #7745: html: inventory is broken if the docname contains a space
* #7902: html theme: Add a new option :confval:`globaltoc_maxdepth` to control
  the behavior of globaltoc in sidebar
* #7052: add ``:noindexentry:`` to the Python, C, C++, and Javascript domains.
  Update the documentation to better reflect the relationship between this option
  and the ``:noindex:`` option.
* #7899: C, add possibility of parsing of some pre-v3 style type directives and
  roles and try to convert them to equivalent v3 directives/roles.
  Set the new option :confval:`c_allow_pre_v3` to ``True`` to enable this.
  The warnings printed from this functionality can be suppressed by setting
  :confval:`c_warn_on_allowed_pre_v3`` to ``True``.
  The functionality is immediately deprecated.

Bugs fixed
----------

* #7886: autodoc: TypeError is raised on mocking generic-typed classes
* #7935: autodoc: function signature is not shown when the function has a
  parameter having ``inspect._empty`` as its default value
* #7901: autodoc: type annotations for overloaded functions are not resolved
* #904: autodoc: An instance attribute cause a crash of autofunction directive
* #1362: autodoc: ``private-members`` option does not work for class attributes
* #7839: autosummary: cannot handle umlauts in function names
* #7865: autosummary: Failed to extract summary line when abbreviations found
* #7866: autosummary: Failed to extract correct summary line when docstring
  contains a hyperlink target
* #7469: autosummary: "Module attributes" header is not translatable
* #7940: apidoc: An extra newline is generated at the end of the rst file if a
  module has submodules 
* #4258: napoleon: decorated special methods are not shown
* #7715: LaTeX: ``numfig_secnum_depth > 1`` leads to wrong figure links
* #7846: html theme: XML-invalid files were generated
* #7894: gettext: Wrong source info is shown when using rst_epilog
* #7691: linkcheck: HEAD requests are not used for checking
* #7928: py domain: failed to resolve a type annotation for the attribute
* #7968: i18n: The content of ``math`` directive is interpreted as reST on
  translation
* #7869: :rst:role:`abbr` role without an explanation will show the explanation
  from the previous abbr role
* C and C++, removed ``noindex`` directive option as it did
  nothing.
* #7619: Duplicated node IDs are generated if node has multiple IDs

Testing
--------

{"file_path": "/workspace/regressions/test_index_symbols.py", "content": """"Regression tests for grouping of symbol index entries.

See: "Two sections called Symbols in index".  Symbol entries whose leading
character lies after the ASCII letters (such as ``£`` and ``←``) used to be
sorted *after* the alphabetic entries, which produced a second ``Symbols``
group with the same HTML anchor as the first one.
"""

import pytest

from sphinx.environment.adapters.indexentries import IndexEntries
from sphinx.testing import restructuredtext
from sphinx.testing.path import path

pytest_plugins = 'sphinx.testing.fixtures'


@pytest.fixture(scope='session')
def rootdir():
    return path(__file__).parent.parent / 'tests' / 'roots'


@pytest.mark.sphinx('dummy', freshenv=True)
def test_symbols_are_grouped_into_single_section(app):
    text = (".. index:: @decorator\n"
            ".. index:: £pound\n"
            ".. index:: ←arrow\n"
            ".. index:: docutils\n")
    restructuredtext.parse(app, text)
    index = IndexEntries(app.env).create_index(app.builder)

    keys = [key for key, _ in index]
    # all symbol entries must share one single "Symbols" section
    assert keys.count('Symbols') == 1
    # ... and that section has to come before the alphabetic ones
    assert keys[0] == 'Symbols'
    assert keys[1] == 'D'

    symbols = dict(index)['Symbols']
    assert [name for name, _ in symbols] == ['@decorator', '£pound', '←arrow']


@pytest.mark.sphinx('dummy', freshenv=True)
def test_symbols_grouping_matches_low_ascii_symbols(app):
    text = (".. index:: 9-symbol\n"
            ".. index:: &-symbol\n"
            ".. index:: £-symbol\n"
            ".. index:: docutils\n")
    restructuredtext.parse(app, text)
    index = IndexEntries(app.env).create_index(app.builder)

    keys = [key for key, _ in index]
    assert keys == ['Symbols', 'D']
    symbols = dict(index)['Symbols']
    assert [name for name, _ in symbols] == ['&-symbol', '9-symbol', '£-symbol']
"}
